test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 14 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Meera purchased 23 bracelets at ₹160 each. At what rate per bracelet must she sell them to earn a 15% profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The total quantity (23 bracelets) is redundant data for per-unit rate calculations.

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) × 1.15

SP = 160 × 1.15

SP = 184

**∴ The correct answer is ₹184.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of 1 bracelet = ₹160

Total number of bracelets = 23

Desired Profit = 15%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × [(100 + Profit%) ÷ 100]

 
 Total CP = ₹3680 
 + 15% Profit Total SP = ₹4232 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Cost Price (CP) for 23 bracelets = 160 × 23 = ₹3680

⇒ Total Selling Price (SP) for 15% profit = 3680 × [(100 + 15) ÷ 100]

⇒ Total SP = 3680 × (115 ÷ 100)

⇒ Total SP = 3680 × 1.15 = ₹4232

⇒ SP per bracelet = Total SP ÷ Total Bracelets

⇒ SP per bracelet = 4232 ÷ 23 = ₹184

**∴ The correct answer is ₹184.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Base of Profit/Loss Calculation

Profit and loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise. Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Direct Multiplier Method

To calculate the Selling Price directly, multiply the Cost Price by the multiplying factor. For a profit of P%, SP = CP × (100 + P) ÷ 100.

Redundant Data in Rate Problems

When all items are bought and sold at identical rates, the uniform profit or loss percentage applies exactly the same way to a single item as it does to the entire batch. The total quantity is therefore unnecessary for finding the rate per item.
